name: Merz b. Schwanen
why: Thirty-two loopwheelers still running in Albstadt — the 1911 jersey, remade.
origin: Balthasar Merz, Albstadt in the Swabian Alb, 1911 — loopwheeled workers’ shirts and undergarments, shut down by his descendants. Gitta and Peter Plotnicki found a ninety-year-old Henley at a Berlin flea market in 2011, traced the name, were offered it, and spent a year restoring the machines.
opview: Says it designs and crafts original, consciously made clothing for those who appreciate quality materials and timeless design.

onething.n: verified — 100% organic cotton, 2-thread loopwheeled jersey at 245g, made in Albstadt, $120. The house has no 215-only collection, so the ORIGINALS page is linked; the 215 sits first on it

notes.cotton: 100 of 119 clothing styles are mainly cotton, and every German-made piece is jersey or fleece knit on loopwheelers or 1960s machines
notes.craft: 32 original loopwheelers on a 130-square-metre floor in Albstadt, the newest built in the 1960s and the oldest in 1889 — the house states the count itself
notes.tech: nothing licensed and no elastane in any clothing style. The only stretch in the range is a swim lining and one sock
notes.briish: German end to end on the ORIGINALS side; the rest is made in Portugal
notes.dur: the German line is 2-thread and 2-thread heavy loopwheeled jersey at up to 245g, which is roughly double a standard tee

cities: Two own stores — Canal Street and Abbot Kinney — plus 89 US stockists

marks: A complete HOUSE fabric-naming system, stated on a dedicated /pages/fabrics page and carried onto the PDPs, with NOT ONE (R) or (TM) glyph anywhere. Made-in-Germany originals, each named with a weight: 'Cotton 1-Thread' (100% organic cotton, 4.6oz/sq.yd, 155g/sqm, loopwheeled, no side seams), 'Cotto
